fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: A broken tooth can happen in a moment, from biting into something hard, a fall or a knock during sport. Some breaks are small and painless, while others expose the inner layers of the tooth and cause significant discomfort. At Precision Dental, we assess broken teeth promptly and discuss the most suitable way to repair and protect them.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Is a Broken Tooth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A broken tooth can range from a minor chip in the enamel to a crack that extends into the root. Common types include:

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Chipped teeth, where a small piece of enamel breaks away

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Cracked teeth, where a crack runs through the tooth, sometimes without visible separation

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Fractured cusps, where part of the chewing surface breaks off, often around a large filling

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Split teeth, where a tooth divides into separate segments

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Vertical root fractures, which start in the root and may not be visible

fields.label: Text
fields.value: Important

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: When to Seek Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Even if a break is not painful, it is best to have it checked, as cracks can progress. Contact us promptly if you have:

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Sharp pain or sensitivity to hot, cold or sweet foods

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Pain when biting or releasing your bite

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A sharp edge cutting your tongue or cheek

fields.label: List item
fields.value: A large piece of tooth missing

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Bleeding or swelling

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: If a tooth has been broken during a significant injury involving your head or jaw, seek medical care first by calling 000 or going to your nearest hospital emergency department.

sections.label: What to Do Before Your Appointment

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What to Do Before Your Appointment

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Rinse your mouth gently with warm water. If there is bleeding, apply gentle pressure with clean gauze. Keep any broken pieces in milk or saliva and bring them with you. Use a cold compress to reduce swelling, avoid chewing on the affected side, and take over-the-counter pain relief as directed if suitable. Dental wax or sugar-free gum can temporarily cover a sharp edge.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Happens at Your Appointment

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We examine the tooth, check for cracks and take digital X-rays to assess the nerve and roots. We then explain the extent of the damage and your options. A small chip may be smoothed or repaired with a white filling or composite resin veneers. Larger breaks may need a crown, which can often be made in one visit with our CEREC same-day crown system. If the nerve is affected, root canal therapy may be required. Where a tooth cannot be restored, we discuss removal and replacement options.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Aftercare and Ongoing Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Avoid biting hard foods on the repaired tooth, particularly in the first 24 hours. Some sensitivity may occur for a short time. If you play sport, a custom mouthguard helps protect your teeth, and if you grind your teeth, a night splint may reduce the risk of further fractures.

sections.label: Why Choose Precision Dental for a Broken Tooth

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Why Choose Precision Dental for a Broken Tooth

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We offer urgent appointments, digital imaging and in-house CEREC technology, which allows many broken teeth to be restored with a ceramic crown in a single visit. We always explain the options clearly, from the most conservative approach onwards.

sections.label: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The cost of your treatment depends on your individual needs. After your examination, we talk you through your options and the expected fees before any treatment begins. We accept most major health funds, process claims on the spot through HICAPS and are a preferred provider for {{site:preferredFunds}}. Interest-free payment plans are available through DentiCare for eligible patients, subject to terms and conditions. You can learn more on our Prices and Payment Options page.

fields.label: Small label
fields.value: FAQ

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Frequently Asked Questions

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Is a chipped tooth an emergency?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A small chip without pain is not usually urgent, but it should be checked soon. Pain, bleeding or a large break should be seen as soon as possible.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can a cracked tooth heal on its own?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: No. Unlike bone, teeth cannot repair cracks. Early treatment can help prevent a crack from spreading.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can you reattach a broken piece of tooth?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: In some cases, a fragment can be bonded back into place. Keep it moist in milk or saliva and bring it to your appointment.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Will I need a crown?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: It depends on the size and location of the break. Small chips can often be repaired with a filling, while larger fractures may need a crown.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: What if my broken tooth does not hurt?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A break may not hurt at first, but cracks can progress or allow bacteria to reach the nerve. An assessment is still recommended.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can a broken tooth be fixed on the same day?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Many repairs, including fillings and CEREC crowns, can be completed on the same day, depending on the damage.
